records.source: וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר־יְהוָ֛ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ שֵׁנִ֑ית וְהוּא֙ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ עָצ֔וּר בַּחֲצַ֥ר הַמַּטָּרָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah a second [time], and he still [was] shut up in [the] courtyard of the guard, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still held in the courtyard of the guard:

L.1: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah a second time, while he [was] still shut up in the courtyard of the guard, saying:

R.1: Jeremiah was still locked up in the courtyard of the guard. While he was there, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave him a second message:

decisions.choice: a second time: a second word in the same setting as chapter 32
decisions.reason: The first word came while Jeremiah was held in the courtyard of the guard during the siege (32:1-2, 6, 26). This second word comes while he is still there, and it carries on the promises of 32:36-44 that the city and land will be restored.

decisions.choice: shut up in the courtyard of the guard: held under watch within the palace
decisions.reason: As in 32:2, where the place is explained: a guarded court in the royal palace where Jeremiah was confined but could still receive visitors and speak (32:8, 12; 37:21; 38:28).

decisions.choice: courtyard of the guard (all levels); shut up (L), held (B), locked up (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of 32:2 at each level. Readable puts the setting first and says "gave him a second message" for "the word came", following the wording set for this formula in Jeremiah.

records.heading: Healing for the city

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עֹשָׂ֑הּ יְהוָ֗ה יוֹצֵ֥ר אוֹתָ֛הּ לַהֲכִינָ֖הּ יְהוָ֥ה שְׁמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh [who] made it, Yahweh who formed it to establish it, Yahweh [is] his name:
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who made it, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who formed it and set it firm; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name:

L.2: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who made it, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who formed it to establish it, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name:

R.2: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made it, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shaped it and made it stand firm. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. He says:

decisions.choice: it: the Hebrew names no object for what the LORD made, formed and established
decisions.reason: The three verbs each have "it" (a feminine pronoun) with no noun to point back to. It may mean the earth, which the LORD made and set firm (10:12; 51:15); the Septuagint has "the earth" here. Or it may mean what the LORD plans and then carries out, as when he says of the fall of cities, "I formed it ... now I have brought it about" (Isaiah 37:26). The Hebrew is kept as it stands, with "it".

decisions.choice: formed: shaped, as a potter shapes clay; establish: make firm so that it stands
decisions.reason: The verb "form" is the potter's word (18:4-6; Genesis 2:7). "Establish" means to set something firmly in place so that it lasts.

decisions.choice: the LORD is his name: a phrase from Israel's hymns
decisions.reason: The words close the praise of God as Creator in Amos 5:8 and 9:6 and are sung in Exodus 15:3. Jeremiah uses the longer form "the LORD of hosts is his name" in 10:16 and 31:35. The God who speaks is the one whose word made the world.

decisions.choice: short sentences; "it" kept
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the titles into short sentences but keeps "it" unexplained, because the Hebrew does not say what "it" is (m1).

records.source: קְרָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וְאֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ וְאַגִּ֧ידָה לְּךָ֛ גְּדֹל֥וֹת וּבְצֻר֖וֹת לֹ֥א יְדַעְתָּֽם׃ס
records.gloss: Call to me and I will answer you, and I will tell to you great [things] and inaccessible [things] [which] not you have known them.
pieces: Call out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will answer you. I will make known to you great things, things beyond your reach, which you have not known.

L.3: Call to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will answer you, and I will tell you great [things] and inaccessible [things] that you have not known.

R.3: Call to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will answer you. I will tell you about great things that are out of your reach, things you do not know.

decisions.choice: inaccessible things: things fenced off, out of human reach
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for cities with high walls that no one can get into (Numbers 13:28; Deuteronomy 3:5). Said of things, it means matters closed off from human knowing until God opens them. A few Hebrew manuscripts have a word that differs by one letter, "guarded" or "hidden things", the word used in Isaiah 48:6 for new things God has kept back; the sense is close either way. The Septuagint has "strong things", a reading of the same consonants as "fortified". The usual Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: you: one person, Jeremiah himself
decisions.reason: "Call" and every "you" in this verse are singular. The LORD speaks to the prophet in prison: if he prays, God will answer him and show him what no one could know.

decisions.choice: call and I will answer: the promise that God hears prayer
decisions.reason: The pairing of call and answer is a promise found in Psalm 91:15 and Isaiah 58:9. Here it is an invitation: what God is about to say of the city's future is beyond what anyone in the siege could see.

decisions.choice: great things, things out of reach
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the picture of the word (m1) in plain terms rather than the more general "hidden". Literal says "inaccessible".

records.source: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַל־בָּתֵּי֙ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְעַל־בָּתֵּ֖י מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה הַנְּתֻצִ֕ים אֶל־הַסֹּלְל֖וֹת וְאֶל־הֶחָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel concerning [the] houses of the city the this and concerning [the] houses of [the] kings of Judah, the [ones] torn down against the siege ramps and against the sword:
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this about the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah, which have been torn down to hold back the siege ramps and the sword:

L.4: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city and concerning the houses of the kings of Judah that are torn down against the siege ramps and against the sword:

R.4: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says. He speaks about the houses in this city and the houses of Judah's kings. They have been torn down to make the defenses stronger against the enemy's ramps and swords.

decisions.choice: houses torn down: buildings pulled apart to strengthen the city's defenses
decisions.reason: During a siege the defenders took down houses near the wall and used their stones and timber to make it thicker and higher. Isaiah 22:10 describes the same thing in an earlier siege of Jerusalem. Even the royal houses were sacrificed.

decisions.choice: against the siege ramps and against the sword: torn down to stand against the enemy's ramps and weapons
alternatives: torn down by the siege ramps and the sword
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that the houses were torn down "against" the ramps and the sword. Most naturally the houses were taken apart to build defenses against the attack. It could also mean that they were broken down by the ramps and weapons of the attackers. Either way the ruined houses stand for a city that is losing the fight.

decisions.choice: siege ramps: mounds of earth heaped against a wall
decisions.reason: Attackers built ramps up to a city wall so that soldiers and battering rams could reach the top (6:6; 32:24; Isaiah 37:33).

decisions.choice: to hold back (B); to make the defenses stronger (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why the houses were torn down, following m2. Literal keeps the bare "against". Readable also adds "enemy's" to make clear whose ramps and swords they are.

records.source: בָּאִ֗ים לְהִלָּחֵם֙ אֶת־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּלְמַלְאָם֙ אֶת־פִּגְרֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הִכֵּ֥יתִי בְאַפִּ֖י וּבַחֲמָתִ֑י וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר הִסְתַּ֤רְתִּי פָנַי֙ מֵהָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את עַ֖ל כָּל־רָעָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: [They are] coming to fight with the Chaldeans and to fill them [with] corpses of the human [beings] whom I have struck down in my anger and in my wrath, and [as] I have hidden my face from the city the this because of all their evil.
pieces: They come to fight against the Chaldeans, but only to fill these houses with the dead bodies of the people I have struck down in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rage; for I have hidden {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from this city because of all their evil.

L.5: [They are] coming to fight with the Chaldeans, and to fill them with the corpses of the people whom I have struck down in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath, and [as] I have hidden {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from this city because of all their evil.

R.5: Men are going out to fight the Babylonians. But they will only fill these houses with the dead bodies of the people I have struck down because I am so angry. I have turned away from this city because of all the evil its people have done.

decisions.choice: coming to fight the Chaldeans: the defenders go out against the Babylonians
alternatives: the Chaldeans are coming to fight
decisions.reason: The verse begins with a bare "coming", with no subject. Most likely it means the men of Jerusalem who go to fight the Chaldeans, and the result is only more dead. The Hebrew sentence is hard, and some read it as the Chaldeans coming to fight against the city. The text is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: to fill them: to fill the houses of verse 4 with the dead
decisions.reason: "Them" points back to the houses. The houses taken apart for the defense will be filled with the bodies of those who die in the fighting.

decisions.choice: I have hidden my face: I have turned away and will not help
decisions.reason: To hide the face is to withdraw favor and protection (Deuteronomy 31:17-18; Isaiah 8:17; 54:8). The city is left to its enemies because of its evil.

decisions.choice: and whom ... and as I have hidden: the small word links the hiding of God's face to the slaughter
decisions.reason: The word usually means "which" or "whom". Here it is best taken as giving the reason or the setting: the people die because God has hidden his face from the city.

decisions.choice: but only to fill (B); But they will only fill (R); these houses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that the fighting achieves nothing but more dead, and say that "them" means the houses (m2).

records.source: הִנְנִ֧י מַעֲלֶה־לָּ֛הּ אֲרֻכָ֥ה וּמַרְפֵּ֖א וּרְפָאתִ֑ים וְגִלֵּיתִ֣י לָהֶ֔ם עֲתֶ֥רֶת שָׁל֖וֹם וֶאֱמֶֽת׃
records.gloss: Here I [am] bringing up to it healing and cure, and I will heal them; and I will reveal to them an abundance of peace and stability.
pieces: But look, I will bring this city recovery and a cure. I will heal its people and show them peace and stability in abundance.

L.6: Look, I am going to bring up for it healing and cure, and I will heal them; and I will reveal to them an abundance of peace and stability.

R.6: But I will make this city well again. I will heal its people, and I will let them enjoy peace and safety in plenty.

decisions.choice: I am going to bring up healing: the answer to the question of 8:22
decisions.reason: In 8:22 Jeremiah asked why the healing of his people had not "come up". The same words, the verb and the noun, return here: now God himself will bring the healing up. The word means new flesh growing over a wound, and so recovery (30:17; Isaiah 58:8).

decisions.choice: abundance: a rare word, a wealth or plenty
decisions.reason: The noun occurs only here. It comes from a verb meaning to be plentiful, and most take it as abundance. The sense of the line is clear: God will show his people peace in full measure.

decisions.choice: peace and stability: well-being that lasts
decisions.reason: The second word is the one that means faithfulness or truth. With "peace" it means firmness and security, as in Isaiah 39:8, where the same pair of words is used. The false prophets had promised "true peace" (14:13); now God gives it.

decisions.choice: this city, its people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom "it" (the city) and "them" (its people) refer to.

records.source: וַהֲשִֽׁבֹתִי֙ אֶת־שְׁב֣וּת יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת שְׁב֣וּת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבְנִתִ֖ים כְּבָרִֽאשֹׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will turn back [the] fortunes of Judah and [the] fortunes of Israel, and I will build them as at the first.
pieces: I will restore the fortunes of Judah and of Israel, and I will rebuild them as they were at the beginning.

L.7: And I will restore the fortunes of Judah and the fortunes of Israel, and I will build them as at the first.

R.7: I will make things good again for Judah and for Israel. I will build them up again, as they were before.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes: turn the people's ruin around
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats one root: "turn the turning". It means a full change from ruin back to well-being (Deuteronomy 30:3; Job 42:10). Some take the noun as "captivity", "bring back the captives", which suits the exile; the promise of rebuilding follows either way. Jeremiah uses the phrase again in 33:11 and 33:26, and in 29:14, 30:3 and 32:44.

decisions.choice: Judah and Israel: both kingdoms, south and north
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom, Israel, had gone into exile long before (2 Kings 17). The promise takes in the whole nation again, as in 23:6 and 30:3.

decisions.choice: I will build them: the building promised at Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: God made Jeremiah his messenger "to build and to plant" as well as to tear down (1:10). The promise to build the people up again returns in 24:6 and 31:4, 28.

decisions.choice: make things good again
decisions.reason: Readable says what "restore the fortunes" means in plain words, as Deuteronomy 30:3 does.

records.source: וְטִ֣הַרְתִּ֔ים מִכָּל־עֲוֺנָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָֽטְאוּ־לִ֑י וְסָלַחְתִּ֗י לְכָל־עֲוֺנֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָֽטְאוּ־לִ֔י וַאֲשֶׁ֖ר פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity which they have sinned against me, and I will forgive all their iniquities which they have sinned against me and which they have rebelled against me.
pieces: I will cleanse them from all the guilt of their sin against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will forgive all their guilt, every way they have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.8: And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity by which they have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will forgive all their iniquities by which they have sinned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and by which they have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.8: I will wash away all the sins they have done against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will forgive all their sins and every way they have turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: iniquity, sin, rebellion: every kind of wrong
decisions.reason: Three words for wrongdoing are piled up: iniquity (the guilt of crooked deeds), sin (missing the mark) and rebellion (breaking away from one's master). Together they say that nothing the people have done is left out of the cleansing and forgiveness.

decisions.choice: cleanse and forgive: the promise of the new covenant
decisions.reason: In 31:34 God promised, "I will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more." Here forgiveness is joined with cleansing, the washing away of what made the people unclean before God (2:22; 13:27).

decisions.choice: all: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text spells the word for "all" slightly differently from the form the scribes noted in the margin to be read aloud. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "iniquity"; Balanced says "guilt" and Readable "sins", the wording set for this word in the prophets. Readable says "wash away" for "cleanse".

records.source: וְהָ֣יְתָה לִּ֗י לְשֵׁ֤ם שָׂשׂוֹן֙ לִתְהִלָּ֣ה וּלְתִפְאֶ֔רֶת לְכֹ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁמְע֜וּ אֶת־כָּל־הַטּוֹבָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָֽנֹכִי֙ עֹשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם וּפָחֲד֣וּ וְרָֽגְז֗וּ עַ֤ל כָּל־הַטּוֹבָה֙ וְעַ֣ל כָּל־הַשָּׁל֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָֽנֹכִ֖י עֹ֥שֶׂה לָּֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: And it will be to me for a name of joy, for praise and for glory to all [the] nations of the earth who will hear all the good that I [am] doing [for] them; and they will fear and tremble because of all the good and because of all the peace that I [am] doing for it.
pieces: This city will be for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a name of joy, praise and glory before all the nations of the earth. They will hear of all the good I do for its people, and they will be in awe and tremble because of all the good and all the peace I bring about for it.

L.9: And it will be to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a name of joy, a praise and a glory before all the nations of the earth, who will hear of all the good that I am doing for them; and they will fear and tremble because of all the good and because of all the peace that I am making for it.

R.9: Then this city will give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a name that brings joy, praise and honor among all the nations of the earth. They will hear about all the good things I do for its people. They will be amazed and shake with awe because of all the good things and the peace I give the city.

decisions.choice: a name, a praise and a glory: what Israel was meant to be
decisions.reason: In 13:11 God said he had bound his people to himself like a belt, to be for him "a people, a name, a praise and a glory", but they would not listen. Deuteronomy 26:19 uses the same words. What the people failed to be, the restored city will become.

decisions.choice: it: the city; them: its people
decisions.reason: The verb "it will be" is feminine, pointing back to "this city" (verses 4-5). "Them" in "doing for them" are its people, and "it" at the end is the city again.

decisions.choice: fear and tremble: be shaken with awe
decisions.reason: The nations will not fear harm; they will be overwhelmed by the greatness of what God does. The first verb is used of a heart that thrills with wonder in Isaiah 60:5, and of turning in awe to the LORD in Hosea 3:5.

decisions.choice: this city, its people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the city and its people (m2). Readable says "a name that brings joy" for "a name of joy" and "amazed and shake" for "fear and tremble" (m3).

records.source: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עוֹד֮ יִשָּׁמַ֣ע בַּמָּקוֹם־הַזֶּה֒ אֲשֶׁר֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים חָרֵ֣ב ה֔וּא מֵאֵ֥ין אָדָ֖ם וּמֵאֵ֣ין בְּהֵמָ֑ה בְּעָרֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ וּבְחֻצ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הַֽנְשַׁמּ֗וֹת מֵאֵ֥ין אָדָ֛ם וּמֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵׁ֖ב וּמֵאֵ֥ין בְּהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: again will be heard in the place the this, which you [are] saying, desolate [is] it, without human and without animal, in [the] cities of Judah and in [the] streets of Jerusalem that [are] desolated, without human and without inhabitant and without animal,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Once more there will be heard in this place, which you call a ruin with neither people nor animals, in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem that lie deserted, without people, without anyone living there, without animals,

L.10: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: There will again be heard in this place, of which you are saying, 'It [is] a waste, without human or animal,' in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate, without human and without inhabitant and without animal,

R.10: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: You say that this place is a ruin, with no people or animals in it. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are empty. No people live there, and there are not even any animals. But you will hear sounds there again.

decisions.choice: a waste, without people or animals: the people's own words about the land
decisions.reason: In 32:43 the people say of the land, "It is a desolation, without people or animals." God takes up their words of despair and answers them with a promise.

decisions.choice: will be heard: the sentence runs on into verse 11
decisions.reason: What will be heard again is listed in verse 11: the sounds of joy, of weddings and of thanksgiving. Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma.

decisions.choice: the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem: the places named in the threat of 7:34
decisions.reason: God had said he would silence joy "in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem" (7:34; compare 44:6). The same places are named here for the promise that turns the threat around.

decisions.choice: But you will hear sounds there again.
decisions.reason: Readable puts the people's words first in short sentences, then says what will happen, so that verse 11 can begin a new sentence.

records.source: ק֣וֹל שָׂשׂ֞וֹן וְק֣וֹל שִׂמְחָ֗ה ק֣וֹל חָתָן֮ וְק֣וֹל כַּלָּה֒ ק֣וֹל אֹמְרִ֡ים הוֹדוּ֩ אֶת־יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת כִּֽי־ט֤וֹב יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֔וֹ מְבִאִ֥ים תּוֹדָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־אָשִׁ֧יב אֶת־שְׁבוּת־הָאָ֛רֶץ כְּבָרִאשֹׁנָ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: [the] sound of joy and [the] sound of gladness, [the] voice of bridegroom and [the] voice of bride, [the] voice of [those] saying, Give thanks to Yahweh of hosts, for good [is] Yahweh, for to forever [is] his loyal love, bringing thank offering [to the] house of Yahweh; for I will turn back [the] fortunes of the land as at the first, says Yahweh.
pieces: the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bridegroom and bride, and the voices of those who say, 'Give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies thanks, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is good; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever,' as they bring offerings of thanks to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as they were at the beginning, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.11: the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those saying, 'Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] good, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever,' bringing thank offering [to] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as at the first, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.11: You will hear the sounds of joy and happiness and the happy voices of a bride and groom at their wedding. You will hear people singing, 'Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is good! His faithful love lasts forever.' They will sing as they bring offerings to thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple. I will make things good again for the land, as they were before, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the sound of joy and gladness, of bridegroom and bride: the threat of 7:34 turned around
decisions.reason: God had said he would silence these very sounds (7:34; 16:9; 25:10). Weddings were the most joyful times of town life, and their silence meant that ordinary life had ended. Now God promises that they will be heard again.

decisions.choice: Give thanks to the LORD ... his loyal love is forever: the refrain of Israel's worship
decisions.reason: These are the words that open Psalms 106, 107, 118 and 136 and that were sung when the ark came to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 16:34) and when the second temple's foundation was laid (Ezra 3:11). Here the call names "the LORD of hosts" and then says "the LORD is good". The temple's songs will be sung again.

decisions.choice: loyal love: faithful, covenant love
decisions.reason: The word is the love that keeps faith within a bond, God's commitment to his people that does not give up.

decisions.choice: thank offering: an offering given to thank God
decisions.reason: The word means both thanks and the offering that expresses it (17:26; Leviticus 7:12-15). Those who sing the refrain bring their thanks with them to the temple.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes of the land: as in verse 7
decisions.reason: As in verse 7. Here the whole land is restored as it was at the beginning.

decisions.choice: the wording of 7:34 at each level
decisions.reason: The sounds of joy and of bride and bridegroom are worded as in 7:34 and 16:9, so that the promise is heard as the reversal of the threat. Readable adds "singing" for the voices that say the refrain.

decisions.choice: the refrain worded as Psalm 136:1 and 1 Chronicles 16:34
decisions.reason: The call to thanks keeps the wording of the psalms at each level: "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced and "faithful love" at Readable, with "the LORD of hosts" (Literal) and "the LORD of Armies" (Balanced, Readable) in place of the plain divine name, and "the LORD" in place of "he" before "is good". The thank offering is worded as in 17:26.

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֒ ע֞וֹד יִֽהְיֶ֣ה׀בַּמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה הֶחָרֵ֛ב מֵֽאֵין־אָדָ֥ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֖ה וּבְכָל־עָרָ֑יו נְוֵ֣ה רֹעִ֔ים מַרְבִּצִ֖ים צֹֽאן׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: again there will be in the place the this, the desolate, without human and up to animal, and in all its cities, a pasture of shepherds making flock[s] lie down.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: In this place that lies in ruins, without people or animals, and in all its towns, there will once again be pastures where shepherds rest their flocks.

L.12: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: There will again be in this place, which is a waste, without human or animal, and in all its cities, a pasture for shepherds who make [their] flocks lie down.

R.12: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: This place is now a ruin, with no people or animals. But in it and in all its towns there will again be fields where shepherds let their sheep lie down and rest.

decisions.choice: a pasture where shepherds rest their flocks: a picture of peace in the open country
decisions.reason: Flocks could lie down in the open fields only where no raiders or armies threatened. The land that is now empty of people and animals will be safe grazing land again.

decisions.choice: pasture: grazing land, or the place where shepherds stay
decisions.reason: The word can mean the pasture itself or the camp where shepherds and their flocks settle (23:3; Isaiah 65:10). Both fit here.

decisions.choice: without people or even animals
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "without human and up to animal", that is, without anyone at all, down to the animals. Verse 10 said the same with a different phrase.

decisions.choice: sheep
decisions.reason: Readable says "sheep" for flocks, which included both sheep and goats; Literal and Balanced say "flocks". Readable puts the present ruin first, then the promise.

pieces: In the towns of the hill country, of the western foothills and of the Negev, in Benjamin's territory, in the places surrounding Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.13: In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the Shephelah, and in the cities of the Negev, and in the land of Benjamin, and in the places around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, the flocks will again pass under the hands of the one who counts [them], says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.13: In the towns of the hill country, of the foothills in the west and of the Negev desert in the south, in the land of Benjamin, in the villages near Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah, shepherds will once again count their sheep as they pass by, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the hill country ... the towns of Judah: every region of the land
decisions.reason: The same list of regions is given in 17:26 and 32:44, where it is explained: the central hills, the Shephelah (the low hills to the west), the dry Negev to the south, Benjamin to the north, and the places around Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: pass under the hands of the one who counts: shepherds counting their animals
decisions.reason: At the end of the day a shepherd counted his flock as the animals passed one by one under his hand or his staff, to see that none were missing (Leviticus 27:32; Ezekiel 20:37). The picture is of ordinary, peaceful work in the land again.

decisions.choice: the Shephelah (L); the western foothills (B); the foothills in the west, the Negev desert in the south (R)
decisions.reason: As in 17:26: Literal keeps the region's name; Balanced and Readable say where it lies. Readable says plainly that the shepherds count their sheep.

records.gloss: Look, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, and I will establish the word the good which I have spoken to [the] house of Israel and to [the] house of Judah.
pieces: The days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will carry out the good promise I made to the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

L.14: Look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will establish the good word that I have spoken to the house of Israel and to the house of Judah.

R.14: The time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will do the good things I promised to the people of Israel and Judah.

decisions.choice: verses 14-26 are part of the Hebrew text, though the Septuagint lacks them
decisions.reason: The Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation, has no equivalent of verses 14-26, the longest passage of the Hebrew book missing from the Greek (see the note at 1:1). The verses take up the promise of 23:5-6 and add the promises to David's line and to the Levitical priests. This translation follows the Hebrew text throughout.

decisions.choice: the good word: the promise of good
decisions.reason: "The good word" God has spoken is his promise to restore his people (29:10, where the same phrase is used of bringing them back after seventy years; compare 1 Kings 8:56).

decisions.choice: establish the word: make it stand, carry it out
decisions.reason: The verb means to raise up or make something stand. With "word" it means to fulfill a promise, to make it come true (11:5; 29:10).

decisions.choice: the wording of 23:5 at each level
decisions.reason: "Look, days are coming" is worded as in 23:5, the promise these verses take up. Balanced says "promise" for "word", and Readable "the good things I promised".

records.heading: The righteous Branch

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֤ים הָהֵם֙ וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא אַצְמִ֥יחַ לְדָוִ֖ד צֶ֣מַח צְדָקָ֑ה וְעָשָׂ֛ה מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: In the days the those and at the time the that I will cause to sprout for David a branch of righteousness, and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.
pieces: In those days and at that time \q I will make a righteous Branch spring up for David, \q and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.

L.15: In those days and at that time \q I will cause a Branch of righteousness to sprout for David, \q and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.

R.15: At that time I will make a righteous Branch grow from David's family. \q He will do what is just and righteous in the land.

decisions.choice: this verse repeats 23:5 with differences
decisions.reason: 23:5 begins "Look, days are coming" (here in verse 14) and has "I will raise up for David a righteous Branch" and "he will reign as king and act wisely". This verse has "in those days and at that time", "I will cause to sprout" and "a Branch of righteousness", and leaves out the line about his reign. Both end "he will do justice and righteousness in the land".

decisions.choice: a Branch for David: a coming king from David's line
decisions.reason: As in 23:5, where the title is explained: new growth from the family of David, though its kings have failed (Isaiah 11:1; Zechariah 3:8; 6:12).

decisions.choice: cause to sprout: the verb from the same root as Branch
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun share one root: God will make the shoot shoot up. The picture is of new growth from a stump that seemed dead.

decisions.choice: a Branch of righteousness: a righteous Branch
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the two nouns, "branch of righteousness", the usual way of saying "righteous branch". The king will be the rightful heir and will do what is right, as 23:5 says.

decisions.choice: set in lines as 23:5; its wording reused
decisions.reason: The verse repeats the poetic promise of 23:5, so it is set in lines like it, though the chapter around it is prose. Where the Hebrew is the same, the wording of 23:5 is kept at each level; Balanced and Readable say "righteous Branch" as there. Readable says "at that time" once for "in those days and at that time", and "grow from David's family" for "sprout for David".

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֤ים הָהֵם֙ תִּוָּשַׁ֣ע יְהוּדָ֔ה וִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם תִּשְׁכּ֣וֹן לָבֶ֑טַח וְזֶ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרָא־לָ֖הּ יְהוָ֥ה׀צִדְקֵֽנוּ׃ס
records.gloss: In the days the those will be saved Judah, and Jerusalem will dwell in security; and this [is that] which one will call to her: Yahweh [is] our righteousness.
pieces: In those days Judah will be saved, \q and Jerusalem will live in safety. \q And this is the name people will give her: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Is Our Righteousness.'

L.16: In those days Judah will be saved, \q and Jerusalem will dwell in security; \q and this [is what] one will call her: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] our righteousness.'

R.16: At that time Judah will be saved, \q and Jerusalem will live in safety. \q People will call the city by this name: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Is Our Righteousness.'

decisions.choice: differences from 23:6: Jerusalem, not Israel, and the name given to the city
decisions.reason: 23:6 says "in his days", "Israel will dwell in security" and "this is his name", the name of the king. Here it is "in those days", Jerusalem dwells in security, and the name is given "to her", the city. The king and his city bear one name.

decisions.choice: The LORD is our righteousness: the city named for what God does
decisions.reason: As in 23:6, where the name is explained: the LORD himself is the one who puts his people in the right and makes things right. The city that God rebuilds takes its name from him, as the city of Ezekiel 48:35 is called "The LORD is there".

decisions.choice: that one will call her: people will call the city
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject named: "one will call", the Hebrew way of saying "she will be called". "Her" is Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the wording of 23:6, in single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The verse is worded as 23:6 where the Hebrew is the same and set in lines like it. Because the name stands inside the LORD's speech, it takes single quotation marks here. Readable says "the city" for "her".

records.source: כִּי־כֹ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֣ת לְדָוִ֔ד אִ֕ישׁ יֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֥א בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh: not will be cut off for David a man sitting on [the] throne of [the] house of Israel.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: David will always have a man of his line to sit on the throne of the house of Israel.

L.17: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: There will not be cut off for David a man sitting on the throne of the house of Israel.

R.17: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: There will always be a man from David's family to sit on the throne and rule Israel.

decisions.choice: a man on the throne: the promise to David
decisions.reason: God promised David that his line and his throne would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). The words "there will not be cut off for you a man on the throne of Israel" are those of 1 Kings 2:4; 8:25; 9:5, where the promise depends on the kings' faithfulness.

decisions.choice: not be cut off for David: David will never be without an heir
decisions.reason: "Cut off" is used of a family line that dies out. The promise is that David's line will always have someone to take the throne.

decisions.choice: a promise spoken as the kingdom falls
decisions.reason: The words come while Jerusalem is under siege and the last king of Judah is about to lose his throne (32:3-5). The promise looks past the fall to the Branch of verse 15.

decisions.choice: a man of his line (B); a man from David's family (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the man is one of David's descendants, as the idiom implies (m2). Readable turns the negative into "there will always be" and says "rule Israel" for "the throne of the house of Israel".

records.gloss: And for the priests the Levites not will be cut off a man from before me offering up burnt offering and burning grain offering and making sacrifice all the days.
pieces: Nor will the priests, the Levites, ever be without a man who serves in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence, offering burnt offerings, burning grain offerings and making sacrifices for all time."

L.18: And for the priests, the Levites, there will not be cut off a man before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} offering up burnt offering and burning grain offering and making sacrifice all the days."

R.18: And there will always be priests from the tribe of Levi to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They will offer burnt offerings, burn grain offerings and make sacrifices to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for all time."

decisions.choice: the Levitical priests will not lack a man: the covenant of priesthood
decisions.reason: God gave Phinehas, Aaron's grandson, "a covenant of lasting priesthood" for him and his descendants (Numbers 25:13). Malachi 2:4-5 speaks of God's covenant with Levi. The promise to the priests stands beside the promise to David, as verses 21-22 say again.

decisions.choice: the priests, the Levites: priests who belong to the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: This is Deuteronomy's way of naming the priests (Deuteronomy 17:9; 18:1). Verse 21 puts the two words the other way round, "the Levites, the priests"; the same people are meant.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings, grain offerings and sacrifices: the daily worship of the temple
decisions.reason: As in 17:26, where the offerings are explained. "All the days" means always, without a break.

decisions.choice: priests from the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the Levitical priests" means (m2) and turns the negative into "there will always be".

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah:

L.19: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah, saying:

R.19: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah this message:

decisions.choice: a new word to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: A further word begins here, introduced in the third person. Verses 19-26 continue the passage that the Septuagint lacks (see verse 14).

decisions.choice: the wording set for this formula in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: As in 24:4, with "to Jeremiah" for "to me".

records.heading: The covenant with day and night

records.source: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם־תָּפֵ֨רוּ֙ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֶת־בְּרִיתִ֖י הַלָּ֑יְלָה וּלְבִלְתִּ֛י הֱי֥וֹת יֽוֹמָם־וָלַ֖יְלָה בְּעִתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: if you break my covenant [of] the day and my covenant [of] the night, and so that not [there] be daytime and night at their time,
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: If you could break {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with day and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with night, and stop day and night from coming at their set times,

L.20: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: If you could break {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with the day and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with the night, so that there would not be day and night at their time,

R.20: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I have made a covenant with day and with night, so that each comes at its proper time. Could you break that covenant, so that day and night stopped coming?

decisions.choice: my covenant with the day and with the night: God's fixed order for creation
decisions.reason: God's ordering of day and night is called a covenant, a bond he has made and keeps. After the flood he promised that day and night would not cease (Genesis 8:22) and made a covenant with every living creature (Genesis 9:9-17).

decisions.choice: if you can break: a condition that cannot be met
decisions.reason: No one can stop day and night from coming. The condition is impossible, and so is what follows in verse 21: God's covenant with David will not be broken. 31:35-36 makes the same kind of argument.

decisions.choice: at their time: at the time set for them
decisions.reason: Each comes at its own appointed time, morning and evening, without fail.

decisions.choice: the condition as a statement and a question
decisions.reason: Readable first states the covenant, then asks the impossible question, so that the argument is easy to follow.

records.source: גַּם־בְּרִיתִ֤י תֻפַר֙ אֶת־דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י מִהְיֽוֹת־ל֥וֹ בֵ֖ן מֹלֵ֣ךְ עַל־כִּסְא֑וֹ וְאֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֥ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים מְשָׁרְתָֽי׃
records.gloss: also my covenant may be broken with David my servant, from there being to him a son reigning on his throne, and with the Levites the priests my ministers.
pieces: then {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David could also be broken, and he would have no son to reign on his throne; and so could {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with the Levites, the priests who serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.21: then also {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant could be broken, so that he would not have a son reigning on his throne, and [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant] with the Levites, the priests, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ministers.

R.21: Only then could {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David be broken. Only then would he have no son to rule as king after him. And only then could {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with the priests from the tribe of Levi, who serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, be broken.

decisions.choice: my covenant with David my servant: the promise of 2 Samuel 7
decisions.reason: God's promise of a lasting throne to David (2 Samuel 7:12-16) is called a covenant in 2 Samuel 23:5 and Psalm 89:4. Psalm 89:37-38 compares David's throne to the sun and the moon, as this passage compares God's covenant to day and night.

decisions.choice: the Levites, the priests, my ministers: the covenant of priesthood
decisions.reason: As in verse 18 (Numbers 25:13; Malachi 2:4-5). "Ministers" are those who serve God in his house.

decisions.choice: then also my covenant could be broken: the result of the impossible condition
decisions.reason: The sentence completes verse 20: only if day and night could be stopped could these covenants fail.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a slave or servant. Said by God of David, it is a title of honor, so it is "servant" at every level, as in the rest of the prophets.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יִסָּפֵר֙ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְלֹ֥א יִמַּ֖ד ח֣וֹל הַיָּ֑ם כֵּ֣ן אַרְבֶּ֗ה אֶת־זֶ֨רַע֙ דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י וְאֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֖ם מְשָׁרְתֵ֥י אֹתִֽי׃ס
records.gloss: As not can be counted the host of the heavens and not can be measured the sand of the sea, so I will multiply the offspring of David my servant and the Levites ministering me.
pieces: As the stars of the sky cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the descendants of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David and the Levites who serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.22: As the host of the heavens cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the offspring of David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant and the Levites who minister to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.22: No one can count the stars in the sky or measure the sand on the seashore. In the same way, I will make the descendants of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David and the Levites who serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} too many to count."

decisions.choice: the stars and the sand: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham descendants as many as the stars and the sand on the seashore (Genesis 15:5; 22:17; 32:13). The same promise is now made to David's line and to the Levites.

decisions.choice: the host of the heavens: the stars
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means the countless stars. Elsewhere Jeremiah uses it of the stars that the people wrongly worshiped (8:2; 19:13).

decisions.choice: the Levites who minister to me
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "who minister me", with the object marker on "me", an unusual way of saying "who serve me".

decisions.choice: the stars of the sky (B); the stars in the sky (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the host of the heavens is (m2). Readable says "too many to count" for "multiply".

pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah:

L.23: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah, saying:

R.23: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah this message:

decisions.choice: a further word to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: As in verse 19. The last word of the chapter answers what people are saying about Israel and Judah.

decisions.choice: as verse 19
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

records.source: הֲל֣וֹא רָאִ֗יתָ מָֽה־הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ דִּבְּר֣וּ לֵאמֹ֔ר שְׁתֵּ֣י הַמִּשְׁפָּח֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּחַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בָּהֶ֖ם וַיִּמְאָסֵ֑ם וְאֶת־עַמִּי֙ יִנְאָצ֔וּן מִֽהְי֥וֹת ע֖וֹד גּ֥וֹי לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: [Have] not you seen what the people the this have spoken, saying, [the] two the clans which chose Yahweh in them, and he has rejected them? And my people they despise, from being again a nation before them.
pieces: "Have you not seen what these people are saying: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chose two families, and now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has rejected them'? So they look down on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, as if they were no longer a nation in their eyes.

L.24: "Have you not seen what this people have spoken, saying, 'The two clans that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chose, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has rejected them'? And they despise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, [as] no longer a nation before them.

R.24: "Have you heard what these people are saying? They say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chose two families, Israel and Judah, but now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has turned away from them.' So they treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people with scorn. They do not think of them as a nation anymore.

decisions.choice: the two families: Israel and Judah
alternatives: the house of David and the Levites
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a clan, here used of whole peoples, as in Amos 3:1-2, where all Israel is "the whole family" God brought up from Egypt. The two are most likely the two kingdoms, Israel and Judah (3:6-11; 11:10). Some take them as David's line and the Levites, the two chosen houses of verses 17-22, or as Jacob's descendants and David's (verse 26).

decisions.choice: this people: who are speaking is not said
decisions.reason: "This people" in Jeremiah is often Judah itself (14:10-11), and the words may be the people's own despair. But the end of the verse says that "they" despise "my people", which suggests outsiders, perhaps the neighboring nations, mocking them. The Hebrew leaves it open.

decisions.choice: chosen and rejected: the language of covenant
decisions.reason: God chose Israel to be his own people (Deuteronomy 7:6; 14:2). The speakers say that he has now rejected them, as he had warned (7:29; 2 Kings 17:20). God's answer in verses 25-26 is that he will not.

decisions.choice: no longer a nation before them: in their eyes no nation at all
decisions.reason: "Before them" means in their view. They count God's people as finished.

decisions.choice: clans (L); families (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "clans", the usual word for this term. Balanced and Readable say "families", because here the word names whole nations, and "clans" would sound too small.

decisions.choice: two families, Israel and Judah
decisions.reason: Readable names the two families as Israel and Judah, following m1. This is the likeliest meaning, but not certain.

records.source: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם־לֹ֥א בְרִיתִ֖י יוֹמָ֣ם וָלָ֑יְלָה חֻקּ֛וֹת שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָ֖רֶץ לֹא־שָֽׂמְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: if not my covenant [with] daytime and night, [the] fixed laws of heavens and earth not I have set,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: If I had not made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with day and night, if I had not set in place the fixed laws of heaven and earth,

L.25: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: If [there is] not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with day and night, [if] I have not set the fixed laws of heaven and earth,

R.25: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I have made a covenant with day and night. I have set the laws that the sky and the earth must follow. They still stand.

decisions.choice: if I have not made my covenant: another impossible condition
decisions.reason: As in verse 20. God has set day and night and the laws of heaven and earth in place; as surely as he has, he will keep his promise to his people (verse 26). The verb "set" stands at the end and serves both halves of the verse.

decisions.choice: the fixed laws of heaven and earth: the order God gave creation
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for statutes. In 31:35-36 God speaks of "the fixed laws" of moon and stars: only if they failed would Israel cease to be a nation. Compare Job 38:33.

decisions.choice: statements in place of the condition
decisions.reason: Readable states what God has done and adds "They still stand", so that verse 26 can draw the comparison plainly. The meaning of the oath-like condition is kept.

records.source: גַּם־זֶ֣רַע יַעֲקוֹב֩ וְדָוִ֨ד עַבְדִּ֜י אֶמְאַ֗ס מִקַּ֤חַת מִזַּרְעוֹ֙ מֹֽשְׁלִ֔ים אֶל־זֶ֥רַע אַבְרָהָ֖ם יִשְׂחָ֣ק וְיַעֲקֹ֑ב כִּֽי־אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־שְׁבוּתָ֖ם וְרִחַמְתִּֽים׃ס
records.gloss: also [the] offspring of Jacob and David my servant I will reject, from taking from his offspring rulers over [the] offspring of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; for I will turn back their fortunes and I will have compassion on them.
pieces: then I would also reject Jacob's descendants and those of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, and not take rulers from David's line to govern the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Indeed, I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them."

L.26: then also I would reject the offspring of Jacob and of David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, so as not to take from his offspring rulers over the offspring of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes, and I will have compassion on them."

R.26: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Jacob and of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David. I will always choose rulers from David's descendants to rule over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. I will make things good again for them, and I will have mercy on them."

decisions.choice: then I would reject: the result of the impossible condition
decisions.reason: As in verse 21: since the laws of creation stand, God will not reject Jacob's descendants or David's, and he will go on taking rulers from David's line.

decisions.choice: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: the promise to the fathers
decisions.reason: The rulers from David's line will rule over the people descended from the three fathers to whom God first made his covenant (Genesis 17:7; Exodus 2:24). The name Isaac is spelled here with a different letter, as in Amos 7:9, 16 and Psalm 105:9.

decisions.choice: restore their fortunes and have compassion: the promise of verse 7
decisions.reason: As in verse 7 and Deuteronomy 30:3, where the same two promises stand together. Compassion is the tender love of a parent for a child (31:20).

decisions.choice: I will restore: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a slightly different form of the verb "restore" from the one the scribes noted in the margin to be read aloud. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: Indeed (B)
decisions.reason: The small word that begins the last clause can mean "for" or "surely". Balanced says "Indeed", since the clause says what God will do in place of rejecting his people. Readable leaves the word out and says "make things good again" as in verse 7.
